 Judgment
Though this appeal is listed for orders, with the consent of learned counsel for both parties it is taken up for final disposal.

2. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted his arguments that respondent No.1/Smt.Suvarna, W/o Ramesh has played fraud with the appellants before the Tribunal that claim petition filed before the Tribunal without being knowledge of the appellants.

Appellant Nos.1 and 2,
who are parents of the deceased-Ramesh are not made parties to the proceedings in MVC Madappa S/O Gundappa vs Smt. Suvarna W/O Late Ramesh on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151423370/
2 No.239/2014.

sentences.text: The appellants are old aged parents of deceased-Ramesh and they are very much dependents on deceased-Ramesh.

Further it is submitted that the Tribunal has not correctly assessed the income of the deceased and awarded meager compensation under all the heads, which requires modification and seeking enhancement of compensation.
On all these grounds sought for allowing the appeal.

3. Learned counsel on behalf of respondent No.1/Smt.Suvarna w/o Ramesh has submitted his argument that respondent No.1 has no objection to award amount equally to mother of deceased Smt.Sharnamma and respondent No.1/Smt.Suvarna W/o late Ramesh- deceased and sought for enhancement of compensation.

4. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No.3/insurance company has submitted his argument that the Tribunal has passed the impugned judgment and award in accordance with law and that there are no grounds to interfere with the same.
Hence, sought for dismissal of appeal.

5. Having heard both sides, the following points arise for consideration:
 (i) Whether the appellant  No.2/Sharanamma and respondent  No.1/Suvarna are entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?
 (ii) Whether appellant No.2 and respondent  No.1 are equally entitled for  compensation?
(iii) What order/award?

6. My findings to the above points are as under:
Point No.1: Partly Affirmative Point No.2 : Affirmative Point No.3: As per final order RE. POINT NO.1:
7. In para 14 of the judgment the tribunal has assessed the loss of dependency as under:
"14. LOSS OF DEPENDENCY:
This court has already considered the income of the deceased at Rs. 1,08,000/- per annum.

It has also been held that deceased was aged about 30 years, he was married Madappa S/O Gundappa vs Smt. Suvarna W/O Late Ramesh on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151423370/
3

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: having the responsibility to maintain the family.

perhaps, having wife as dependent,
therefore, he was expected to spend 1/3 of his income towards his personal expenses,
therefore, this court may hold 1/3 of his income towards his personal expenses.

This court on deducting 1/3d for his personal expenses, took the loss of dependency at Rs.
72,000/- per annum.
As per Sarla Verma's case, for the age group between 26 to 30 years, 17 multiplier is applicable.

Therefore, on applying 17 multiplier i.e. Rs. 72,000 x 17 = Rs.
12,24,000/- would be the loss of dependency to petitioner no. 1 to 3 which would be just and proper compensation towards loss of dependency."
8.

The tribunal has not taken into consideration as to the future prospects of the deceased as per the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in NATIONAL INSURANCE CO., LTD., VS. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157 and MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. NANU RAM ALIAS CHUHRU RAM & OTHERS reported in 2018 ACJ 2782.

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE CO., LTD., VS. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. NANU RAM ALIAS CHUHRU RAM & OTHERS reported in 2018 ACJ 2782
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As the per the said judgment, 40% has to be added to the income of the deceased, which would come to Rs.9,000/- + 40% = Rs.12,600/-.
Since there are 3 dependents, 1/3rd has to be deducted from the income.
Thus, the appellant No.2 and Respondent No.1 are entitled for compensation of Rs.17,13,600/- (Rs.8,400/- x 12 x 17) towards loss of dependency.

9. Keeping in mind the above decisions, it is just and proper to award the compensation as under:
Sl. Particulars Awarded by Enhanced by No. the Tribunal this Court in in Rs. Rs.
1 Loss of dependency 12,24,000/- 17,13,600/- 2 Loss of estate 20,000/- 15,000/- 3 Transportation of 15,000/- 15,000/-
 dead body  expenses  4 Loss of consortium 10,000/- 80,000/-
 (Rs.40,000/- x 2)
 Total 12,69,000/- 18,23,600/-
10.
Thus, the petitioners are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.18,23,600/- as against Rs.12,69,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Hence, the Appellant No.2 and Respondent No.1 are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.5,54,600/-.
Accordingly, I answer Point No.1 in partly affirmative.

REGARDING APPORTIONMENT OF COMPENSATION:

sentences.text: Respondent No.1/Smt. Suvarna had filed a claim petition against appellants herein.
At that time, appellants - Sri. Madappa and Smt. Sharnamma, who are the parents of the deceased were not impleaded as parties to the proceedings.

The tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.12,69,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till deposit.

The tribunal has passed an order that on deposit of compensation amount, the petitioner i.e., Smt.Suvarna shall deposit 40% of the award amount in fixed deposit in any nationalised bank for a period of 5 years.

Accordingly, 40% of the amount is deposited in the nationalised bank and it is admitted fact that Smt.Suvarna has already received 60% of the compensation amount.
12.
As per the order dated 18.12.2015, this court has passed an order on I.A.No.3/2015 that tribunal shall not disburse the deposited amount in favour of respondent No.1/Smt. Suvarna.
Appellant No.2/Smt. Sharnamma being a mother of deceased, she is entitled for 50% of the award amount and respondent No.1- Smt.
Suvarna who is wife of deceased is also entitled for 50% of the award amount.
Accordingly, appellant Nos.1 and respondent No.1 are entitled for 50% each of the compensation amount. Accordingly I answer point no.2 in Affirmative.

RE. POINT NO.3:
13.

ORDER (1) The appeal is allowed in part.
(2) The judgment and award dated 17.01.2015 passed by the II Addl. MACt and Additional District Jude, Bidar, sitting at Bhalki, in MVC No.239/2014, is modified.
